description: Original synthetic evaluation fixtures separate from public guided examples. Public gold answers; not a sealed external benchmark.
seed: CREATE TABLE customers(id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, name TEXT, region TEXT, email TEXT)
CREATE TABLE orders(id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, customer_id INTEGER REFERENCES customers(id), amount REAL, ordered_at TEXT, status TEXT)
CREATE TABLE refunds(id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, order_id INTEGER REFERENCES orders(id), amount REAL)

cases.question: Which customers have no email? Return their names.
cases.reference_sql: SELECT name FROM customers WHERE email IS NULL

cases.question: List customer names in the South region.
cases.reference_sql: SELECT name FROM customers WHERE region='South'

cases.question: Which customers have never ordered? Return names.
cases.reference_sql: SELECT c.name FROM customers c LEFT JOIN orders o ON c.id=o.customer_id WHERE o.id IS NULL

cases.question: What is the total order amount, including cancelled orders?
Show each region with orders and its total order amount, including cancelled orders. Return region and total.
cases.reference_sql: SELECT c.region,SUM(o.amount) FROM customers c JOIN orders o ON c.id=o.customer_id GROUP BY c.region

cases.question: Show year-month and total order amount for each month including cancelled orders.
cases.reference_sql: SELECT substr(ordered_at,1,7),SUM(amount) FROM orders GROUP BY substr(ordered_at,1,7)

cases.question: Which orders have amounts strictly above 100? Return id and amount.
cases.reference_sql: SELECT id,amount FROM orders WHERE amount>100

cases.question: What is the total amount for paid orders?
cases.reference_sql: SELECT SUM(amount) FROM orders WHERE status='paid'

cases.question: Which customers have total order amounts above 150? Return name and total, including cancelled orders.
cases.reference_sql: SELECT c.name,SUM(o.amount) FROM customers c JOIN orders o ON c.id=o.customer_id GROUP BY c.id HAVING SUM(o.amount)>150

cases.question: List ids of orders with no refund records.
cases.reference_sql: SELECT id FROM orders WHERE NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM refunds WHERE refunds.order_id=orders.id)

cases.question: Return order id and total refunds for each order that has refunds.
cases.reference_sql: SELECT order_id,SUM(amount) FROM refunds GROUP BY order_id

cases.question: For every customer, return name and total order amounts minus refunds. Include cancelled orders and customers with no orders as zero.
cases.reference_sql: SELECT c.name,COALESCE(SUM(o.amount-COALESCE(r.refunded,0)),0) FROM customers c LEFT JOIN orders o ON c.id=o.customer_id LEFT JOIN (SELECT order_id,SUM(amount) AS refunded FROM refunds GROUP BY order_id) r ON r.order_id=o.id GROUP BY c.id

cases.question: List names of customers who placed more than one order.
cases.reference_sql: SELECT c.name FROM customers c JOIN orders o ON c.id=o.customer_id GROUP BY c.id HAVING COUNT(o.id)>1

cases.question: List order ids with amounts above 5000.
cases.reference_sql: SELECT id FROM orders WHERE amount>5000

cases.question: Which region has the highest total order amount? Return only the region, including cancelled orders.
cases.reference_sql: SELECT c.region FROM customers c JOIN orders o ON c.id=o.customer_id GROUP BY c.region ORDER BY SUM(o.amount) DESC LIMIT 1

cases.question: Return total amount of all orders placed in February 2026.
cases.reference_sql: SELECT SUM(amount) FROM orders WHERE ordered_at>='2026-02-01' AND ordered_at<'2026-03-01'

cases.question: Return customer name and order amount for orders in March 2026.
cases.reference_sql: SELECT c.name,o.amount FROM customers c JOIN orders o ON c.id=o.customer_id WHERE o.ordered_at>='2026-03-01' AND o.ordered_at<'2026-04-01'
